gaps: Symlink handling is internally inconsistent between the two halves of the v2 contract. GitTreeEntry.kind treats mode 120000 as a first-class supported type and returns b'symlink', and I confirmed repository_fingerprints happily fingerprints a tree containing a tracked symlink, hashing the link target as the body. fresh_proof_root then refuses that same tree outright as 'proof archive contains an unsafe path'. The result is a repository that can produce a v2 executable fingerprint but can never produce proof for it, so acceptance is unreachable. This is fail-closed and unreachable here because the repository has zero tracked symlinks, but the two halves should agree: either reject 120000 at _git_tree_entries so the failure is uniform and early, or state explicitly that symlink-bearing repositories are fingerprintable but not provable.

Gitlinks fail at _git_tree_entries with 'Git tree contains unsupported tracked types', which means repository_fingerprints itself raises, not just materialization. That is the correct fail-closed direction and it is uniform, unlike the symlink case, but it amounts to an undocumented platform limitation: a repository containing any submodule cannot be fingerprinted at all. Worth one sentence in the delta spec or operator guide so it is discovered by reading rather than by a failed run.

The tracked-symlink rejection reuses the generic archive-safety message 'proof archive contains an unsafe path', which reads as though the archive were malicious. An operator whose repository legitimately tracks a symlink gets a security-flavoured error for a supportability limitation. A distinct message naming tracked symlinks as unsupported would save a real debugging cycle.

LEGACY_TASK_MARKER matches only [ xX] inside the brackets, while the shipped consumers sdd.py task_counts and _drydock_common._pending_and_done match \[\s\], which also accepts a tab or Unicode whitespace as an unchecked box. A line such as '- [<tab>] task' is therefore pending to the real consumers but is neither canonical nor legacy to the projector, so it is passed through and hashed raw. That is safe and conservative — any later change to it moves the executable digest — but the decline guard does not detect every consumer-recognised shape, so the spec wording about legacy-only whitespace is broader than what the guard actually catches. Align the names or the wording so a future reader does not assume the guard is exhaustive.
risks: Injectivity currently rests on every entry contributing exactly four length-prefixed fields with no entry count or terminator. That is sound as written, but it is an invariant of the loop rather than of the format. If a field is ever added conditionally, or an entry type is allowed to emit a different field count, the injectivity argument must be re-derived. A short comment stating the fixed-arity assumption at _update_tree_digest would make that dependency explicit.

The evidence digest's membership is not simply the allowlist: when task projection is applied, the raw committed tasks.md bytes enter the evidence digest, and when it is declined the file contributes to the executable digest only. That is the intended design and both branches are tested, but it means 'packet evidence' has two definitions depending on projection status, which is worth stating where the allowlist is documented.

Task projection deliberately makes lifecycle status invisible to the executable digest while it still drives claimed_done, the Stop hook, and archive readiness. This is the agreed partition and the verifier attests only the executable fingerprint, but it remains true that an unchanged executable identity does not imply unchanged governance state. The packet discloses this; it should stay disclosed through sync and archive.

The Result section records that after the measured runner failures the pilot edited the scoped Owner checkout directly, so fixed-root mutation containment was not exercised for this work. The disclosure is honest and correctly scoped, and it means the containment property is unproven for this candidate rather than proven absent.

Carried and still accurate: the evidence store is user-writable with digests that identify rather than attest, default phase and run envelopes remain uncalibrated, the capability still spans stacked unsynced deltas so supersession reasoning stays manual until archive, and proof-root test behaviour may differ from a Git checkout.

This review reproduced only the focused controller and evidence suites, as instructed. The full adapter, legacy, and parity suites have not been run against this commit, so nothing here speaks to regressions outside those two modules.
